findings.summary: Objective-draft consent never fires on a project with zero active/proposed objectives — Step 0.5's early exit skips the question the draft path hangs off
findings.suggestion: Offer 'Draft an objective for this task?' also on the no-objective branch when the intent is filled in (mission + outcomes present); keep skipping on not_filled_in/invalid.
findings.evidence: plan.md.j2:105 prints `[intent] no objectives — skipping` on not_filled_in/invalid/no active+proposed; the consent bullet (:107) is reachable only after the objective question (:106), which that exit skips.

reasoning.observe: Early-exit bullet precedes the objective question and the consent bullet; PLAN ADR-005/Interview #2 chose proposer location 'both'; the skill route has no objective-count precondition.
reasoning.trace: A project with mission/outcomes and zero objectives takes the early exit on every /hm:plan; the skill route stays reachable.
reasoning.infer: The plan-side draft path cannot produce a project's first objective through the flow S5 documents.
reasoning.conclude: Real but scoped gap: fire consent on the filled-in-but-zero-objective branch too, or document the scope in the SPEC.

findings.summary: Inline code span split across a hard line-wrap (`observed:\n   missed`)
findings.suggestion: Rewrap so `observed: missed` sits on one line.
findings.evidence: Lines 53-55: the backtick span opens before `observed:` and closes after `missed` two lines later.

reasoning.observe: Template line wrap inside a code span.
reasoning.trace: Rendered skill emits a newline + indentation inside the span.
reasoning.infer: Cosmetic; the rendered markdown shows a broken span.

findings.summary: GAP_SKILL_PHRASES_CLAUDE is asserted against both arms — the name implies a target split that does not exist
findings.suggestion: Fold into GAP_SKILL_PHRASES_BOTH or rename to _INVARIANT.
findings.evidence: Lines 248-250: both constants are checked in the same loop for claude and codex; no is_codex branch distinguishes them.

reasoning.observe: Two constants, both checked identically for both targets.
reasoning.infer: A future reader may split them by target by mistake.

findings.summary: LLM-interpolated <title>/<hypothesis> unescaped into an agent-authored Bash line (Step 4.9, both arms)
findings.suggestion: State the escaping rule at the call site: Claude arm double-quote and escape embedded " / $ / backtick; Codex arm single-quote and replace an apostrophe with '\''; or write the arguments to a temp file. Same fix for SKILL.md.j2's --declined.
findings.evidence: plan.md.j2:729 (Codex, single-quoted) / :733 (Claude, double-quoted) built from interview + RESEARCH text; no escaping rule.

reasoning.observe: Step 4.9 substitutes derived free text into a literal Bash line; the gate is 'show the arguments, run once' — a print, not an ask.
reasoning.trace: The agent's Bash tool executes the literal; argparse sees what the shell parsed. Same sink and gate as SKILL.md.j2:59-60.
reasoning.infer: An apostrophe (Codex) or embedded quote / $( (Claude) breaks the literal; both sinks share source and gate.
reasoning.conclude: Same injection class as the prior review's --claim finding (P2); normalized to P2.

findings.summary: Same unescaped-interpolation pattern for --declined "<title>" in the skill's proposing section
findings.suggestion: Apply the same escaping / temp-file rule as the plan.md.j2 finding; fix both sites together.
findings.evidence: `hm world objective new <ID> ... --from-proposal --candidates <N> --declined "<title>"...` with LLM-proposed titles.

reasoning.observe: SKILL.md.j2:59-60 substitutes LLM-proposed candidate titles into a double-quoted Bash argument.
reasoning.trace: Same sink as plan.md.j2:733, gated only by a print.
reasoning.infer: An embedded double quote, $ or backtick in a title escapes the literal.
reasoning.conclude: Second instance of the same sink at the same severity.

findings.summary: Ledger row lands in base before the record it describes reaches base; mitigation is prose-only
findings.suggestion: Keep as documented (ADR-003), but implement the promised 'rows ÷ proposed+approved files' ratio as a computed metric wherever adoption is reported.
findings.evidence: base = resolve_base_root(root); autopilot_ledger.append_event(base, event="objective_proposed", ...) — record just written under root (a task worktree)

reasoning.observe: world.py:1104-1136 writes INTENT-<id>.md under root; _record_proposal (1140-1156) appends the row at base.
reasoning.trace: ADR-003 names this scenario, rejects writing the row in the worktree (task-land drops it); R7 low/low, 'rows are a numerator only'.
reasoning.infer: Deliberate and reviewed, but no code computes the promised ratio — a raw-count consumer inherits the bias silently.
reasoning.conclude: A reviewed, accepted limitation whose stated mitigation is unimplemented; P2, bounded to observability.

findings.summary: gap_report reads the world twice (status_report then load_world) — a TOCTOU composite under a concurrent writer
findings.suggestion: Load once and derive both the status-shaped fields and the gap-only fields from that single World.
findings.evidence: status = status_report(root)  # load_world inside ... world = load_world(root)  # second load; per-outcome rows merge fields from both (world.py:800-807)

reasoning.observe: world.py:784 and :787 load the world independently; :800-807 merge last/target/gap from snapshot 1 with reason/how_measured from snapshot 2.
reasoning.trace: outcome record / assume observe / a peer's proposal write can land between the two loads; no cross-file lock.
reasoning.infer: A row can mix gap: unevaluable from snapshot 1 with reason: measured from snapshot 2.
reasoning.conclude: gap_report should read the world once; unaddressed by any ADR.

findings.summary: new_objective's exists()-then-write is a plain TOCTOU, now reachable via the proposal flow with a derived id (OBJ- + slug)
findings.suggestion: Exclusive create (O_CREAT|O_EXCL) before the atomic write so two racing new calls fail loudly.
findings.evidence: if path.exists(): raise ... _dump_intent(path, ...) — window widened by load_world + validation in between (world.py:1105-1133)

reasoning.observe: world.py:1105 checks existence, the write happens at :1133.
reasoning.trace: Two sessions running plan Step 4.9 for the same slug derive the same id.
reasoning.infer: Both pass the check; the second silently overwrites the first's record and rejected list.
reasoning.conclude: Pre-existing (REVIEW-playbook-alignment d64291c7), now more reachable; still open.

findings.summary: _real_base_rows_before() guards AC-003 with a before/after count on the real shared auto-advance.jsonl, but it is structurally vacuous AND carries the flakiness test_ledger_isolation.py bans for the sibling ledger
findings.suggestion: Drop the real-base comparison (lines 177-179, 183, 204). Replace with a linked-worktree fixture: tmp fake-base repo, git worktree add, run objective new --from-proposal inside the linked worktree, assert the objective_proposed row lands under the fake base's ledger and is absent from the worktree's copy.
findings.evidence: world_fixture.build_root git-inits the root by default; resolve_base_root returns root for any non-linked-worktree root, so _record_proposal can never write outside root here; _REAL_BASE is this checkout's live ledger, which autopilot_caps writes to from real stage activity.

reasoning.observe: test_intent_doc_new.py:174-179 defines the guard against the live ledger; :183/:204 compare counts around the CLI call.
reasoning.trace: The fixture root is its own git toplevel, so resolve_base_root never walks past it; concurrent sessions append to the compared file legitimately.
reasoning.infer: Vacuous (cannot fail for its stated reason) and flaky (fails on unrelated appends) — compounding.
reasoning.conclude: Replace with a linked-worktree fixture that exercises resolve_base_root's worktree branch; remove the shared-file comparison.

findings.summary: test_ac_001_gap_lists_every_objective_state_with_rejected checks eight named keys but never bounds the row's key set — a gap_report that also copies approval into the LLM-facing surface passes unnoticed
findings.suggestion: Assert the exact key set of every objective row (independently spelled out), or at least "approval" not in the active objective's row.
findings.evidence: _GAP_OBJECTIVE_KEYS deliberately excludes approval; OBJ-2 is built approved; the loop asserts only eight per-key equalities.

reasoning.observe: The per-objective loop enumerates eight fields and never compares the row's key set.
reasoning.trace: gap_report is the proposer's LLM-facing read; the omission of approval is a deliberate boundary.
reasoning.infer: Widening the comprehension satisfies every existing assertion while leaking approved_by.

findings.summary: The gap report combines two filesystem snapshots. An outcome added between reads causes KeyError; a changed definition or measurement can produce a reason that contradicts the reported gap and value. Derive the complete report from one loaded World while preserving the public status payload.
findings.evidence: gap_report calls status_report(root), which loads the world, then calls load_world(root) again and indexes status['outcomes'][outcome.id].

findings.summary: The proposal flow conflicts with the skill's answer-gating rule. Following the specialized instructions permits a write before the operator has consented to its exact arguments, including the generated ID and rejected list; following the general rule adds another confirmation round. Explicitly define whether candidate acceptance authorizes these derived arguments, or collect final consent after presenting them. The phrase-order tests currently preserve this ambiguity.
findings.evidence: The general write rule requires showing exact arguments before consent, but proposal step 4 collects answers and step 5 only then shows the arguments and immediately writes.

findings.summary: A user can consent to drafting without the flow ever obtaining the required outcome. The model must then invent an interview decision, ask an unscheduled question, or skip a requested draft. Add an explicit outcome-selection step when consent is recorded, including paths that skip the interview. The render test only checks phrase positions and cannot detect this missing prerequisite.
findings.evidence: Step 4.9 requires '--outcome = the outcome the interview named', but neither the added consent question nor the interview instructions require selecting an outcome. The existing SPEC-inheritance path can also skip the deep interview.

findings.summary: A Git failure during base-root discovery in a linked worktree can silently send the proposal row to the worktree ledger. The append succeeds, so the promised warning never appears, and task-land can remove the event. Verify that base resolution succeeded for a linked worktree and treat unresolved placement as a telemetry failure, preserving the already-written record.
findings.evidence: _record_proposal uses resolve_base_root, whose git helper suppresses failures and whose fallback returns the current checkout. It then explicitly appends to that resolved path.

findings.summary: The claimed real-base isolation oracle watches the wrong ledger when this suite runs in a worktree, as it does here. A leak into the main checkout would pass. Add a temporary main-plus-linked-worktree test asserting that the objective stays in the linked checkout while exactly one event reaches the main ledger, and resolve the actual main checkout for any real-ledger guard.
findings.evidence: _REAL_BASE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] identifies this checkout, not the main worktree. The proposal tests create standalone fixture roots and never exercise a linked-worktree proposal.
